share.

We are now in the third quarter, with the segment contributing 64% to $2.09.

internal services and expand their public cloud offerings.

Cloud providers also added significant Epic capacity in the quarter for personal and enterprise
agents, which are quickly becoming the next killer app for CPUs in the cloud.
Meta's Muse and OpenAI's DOTS illustrate how quickly personal agents are growing, with

Enterprises are moving fast as well, putting agents to work across software development,
supply chain, and IT operations.

adding to accelerator demand while creating a substantial increase in CPU demand.
Adoption is just starting, and we expect demand to grow sharply as agents are deployed
more broadly and take on more complex work.

cloud providers in the quarter, which will ramp over the coming quarters.
Epic's leadership performance and mature ecosystem, proven at scale, have made it the
host CPU of choice for custom accelerators.

In enterprise, Epic's server sell-through was a record, with strong demand from new

services, communications, retail, and healthcare companies.
Existing customers are also making Epic their primary compute platform, extending adoption
from specific workloads to a much larger share of their overall infrastructure.
We began revenue sharing in the first quarter.
We have more than 1,000 shipments of Epic Venice processors in the third quarter, and
the first OEM systems are on track for availability this quarter.
Early demand is the strongest we have seen for any new Epic generation.
Our OEM and ODM partners have committed more than 240 Venice platforms, 20% more than Turin,
and cloud providers are deploying Venice this quarter ahead of instance rollouts planned

new OEM system for our customers.

systems combining Venice and Instinct GPUs that can run agents and models together.
In the all-CPU configuration, a single Helion rack has up to 144 Venice processors with
nearly 74,000 threads, delivering the highest agent density in the industry.
Helion is a new OEM system that has been developed for the first time in the last 20 years.
We are working on developing a new OEM system for our customers.
We are working on developing a new OEM system for our customers.
Every major server OEM and ODM plans to offer Helion with the first systems shipping this
quarter.
Looking more broadly, demand for server compute is accelerating across cloud, enterprise,
agentic, and superintelligence infrastructure.
Epic is the industry's broadest portfolio, spanning all of these markets, with per-socket
leadership for cloud and agents, per-core leadership for enterprise and head nodes,
and memory and I.O. options tuned to each workload.
Venice builds on that leadership with significantly better performance per watt, performance per
core and performance per dollar than any other x86 or ARM server CPU, positioning us to gain
share and significantly grow our server business as the TAM grows to approximately $220 billion
Turning to our data center AI business, Frontier Labs, hyperscalers and cloud providers expanded
instinct deployments for inferencing and training, driving record revenue.
We started shipping MI455X in volume in the quarter and lead customers including Anthropic,
Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle brought their first Helio racks online quickly.
Customers are now running their latest models and workloads on Helios and we are seeing
very strong performance with the initial deployments.
We expect Helios deployments to increase substantially.
In the fourth quarter, as production continues to ramp and HPE, Dell, Lenovo, Supermicro and
other OEM and ODM partners begin shipping systems.
We are very pleased with the overall performance we are seeing at the rack level.
MI455X leads in compute flops, memory capacity and scale out bandwidth.
And as Helios comes to market, it delivers an even larger lead in memory bandwidth and
higher scale up bandwidth than the competition.
We are working closely with our manufacturing and OEM partners to scale production as customers
expand their deployments.
In supercomputing, EuroHPC selected Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC processors for
LumiAI, Europe's next flagship supercomputer planned to come online in the second half
MI430X delivers nearly nine times the double precision performance of the competition,
which is critical for scientific simulations.
As a result, MI430X has now been selected to power next generation systems around the
world and we are well positioned to win additional designs as governments and research centers
plan their next major investments.
In software, we launched Rokom 10 with major enhancements for production deployments at
scale, including faster startup across large GPU clusters and greater resilience for long
running workloads.
Rokom 10 also adds Agentech Performance.
This is a great example of how Rokom 10 can be used to build a large GPU cluster.
Rokom 10 is a very popular tool for performance tuning with Rokom.ai, which profiles workloads,
identifies bottlenecks, and applies and validates improvements, turning weeks of engineering
optimization into hours.
Customers are also using their own agents to optimize models on our open software stack.
For example, Anthropic highlighted that one engineer used Claude to bring up their latest
model on Instinct MI355 XRacks over a single weekend with strong performance.
Our work with Frontier Labs is already enabling their models to handle complex software development
and performance tuning for Instinct.
And as those capabilities continue to improve, the benefits extend to everyone in the AMD ecosystem.
We announced two acquisitions in the quarter to strengthen our superintelligence portfolio.
Talos brings a highly experienced engineering team and specialized silicon built for low latency,
efficient inference.
We plan to integrate their technology across our solutions portfolio to address the growing demand
for low latency superintelligence applications.
World Labs, led by co-founder and CEO Dr. Fei-Fei Li, brings a world-class research team
with expertise in spatial intelligence and models that understand the physical world,
giving us deeper insight into how Frontier models and workloads are evolving.
Fei-Fei will join AMD as chief scientist,
and will be working with us to develop a new model of software and systems for the future.
We expect both acquisitions to close by the end of the year.
Looking ahead, our focus is on execution at scale.
The ramps of Venice, the MI450 series, and Helios are still early,
and all three are on track to grow significantly.
We now expect data center segment revenue growth to accelerate in the fourth quarter,
and full year segment revenue to more than double from 2025.
Our visibility into 2027 also continues to strengthen.
Last quarter, we said we expected annual server revenue to grow more than 70%,
and data center segment revenue to more than double for the year.
Since then, customers have expanded their Epic and Instinct deployment plans,
and we have secured more supply to support that growth.
We now expect server revenue to double year over year in 2027.
And data center AI revenue to grow even faster than we projected 90 days ago.
As a result, we expect data center to be more than 80% of our total revenue in 2027,
and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth.
Looking further out, customer engagements for MI500 continue to progress very well.
Interest is very high, as it is another significant leap forward in performance.
We are working very closely with multiple frontiers,
and we are working closely with our third-tier labs to optimize MI500 for their workloads,
as they plan multi-gigawatt deployments.
Turning to client and gaming, segment revenue decreased 8% year-over-year to $3.7 billion.
In client, revenue increased 7% year-over-year to $2.9 billion,
driven by strong sales of our Ryzen mobile processors.
Commercial is becoming a larger part of our client business,
as large enterprises adopt Ryzen Pro PCs across their entire business,
and the market is growing rapidly.
8 of the 10 largest banks in the world, and 7 of the 10 largest healthcare and automotive companies,
now use Ryzen Pro PCs.
OEMs continue expanding their AMD-based commercial lineups,
from everyday business PCs to high-end workstations.
HP, Lenovo, and others launched the first commercial notebooks and small form factor desktops,
featuring our newest Ryzen AI Max Pro 400 series processors.
These systems deliver workstation-class performance,
and run superintelligence models with up to 300 billion parameters locally.
Looking at the market, PC sell-through slowed late in the quarter,
as higher memory and component costs weighed on demand.
We are managing the business accordingly, aligning sell-in with sell-through,
to keep customer and channel inventory healthy.
In 2027, we are planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit factor.
In this environment, we expect to outperform the market,
as we deliver our Ryzen roadmap and grow our commercial footprint.
In gaming, revenue declined 40% year-over-year to $773 million,
primarily due to lower semi-custom sales as expected at this stage of the console cycle.
Gaming graphics revenue declined year-over-year,
while Radeon GPU channel sell-through increased sequentially.
Beyond gaming, Radeon AI Pro is a new technology,
and its overall revenue grew significantly from the prior quarter,
as more developers choose AMD to run and fine-tune models locally.
We expect strong growth for Radeon AI Pro to continue,
driven by our leadership performance per dollar,
and an open software stack optimized for the latest open-source models.
Turning to our embedded segment, revenue increased 29% year-over-year to $1.1 billion,
the fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating growth.
Demand was very strong across all platforms,
all of our end markets,
led by strong growth with aerospace and defense, automotive, communications, and industrial customers.
Data center build-outs are also driving higher demand for our embedded CPUs
and adaptive SoCs in control plane and optical networking applications.
We remain on track to close more than $18 billion of design wins in 2026,
our third consecutive record year.
Adaptive design wins have increased every year since we acquired Xilinx,
with embedded x86 and semi-custom wins growing even faster.
As these wins ramp over the next few years,
we expect our embedded business to deliver strong double-digit annual revenue growth
and continue outgrowing the market.
In summary, we delivered an excellent third quarter
and expect an even stronger fourth quarter,
as data center and embedded segment growth more than offsets lower client CPU sales.
We entered 2027 with the strongest product portfolio,
and significant customer momentum.
We have worked across our supply chain to secure the wafers, substrates,
advanced packaging, memory, and other key components needed
to support much higher growth next year.
Based on our current visibility,
we now expect revenue to grow more than 80% in 2027,
which is more than twice the long-term financial model we outlined
at our Financial Analyst Day last November.
Data center will be the largest contributor,
driven by expanding Helios deployments and continued Epic Share gates.
We also expect embedded growth to accelerate next year,
driven by adoption of our adaptive and x86 solutions.
Beyond 2027, we are increasing R&D investment across our silicon software
and systems roadmaps, and working closely with our largest customers
to support their ambitious infrastructure plans for the next three to five years.
We are also deepening our collaboration with our supply chain partners
and investing alongside them to secure the long-term capacity
our growth will require.
Taken together, these give us strong confidence in our ability
to sustain exceptional revenue growth for years to come,
with earnings growing even faster.
